## What

Reduce real-OctoPrint integration time through reusable, validated release builds, faster fixture command boundaries and cheaper isolated world startup. Status/context now reflect completed actions during supervision turns, shutdown handlers are installed before readiness is announced, and expired printer-state waits emit bounded, redacted diagnostics.

## Why

Integration jobs are required checks. Time spent waiting on the simulated printer and repeating preparation delays merges and occupies runners needed by other repositories’ releases. These changes reduce that cost while retaining all seven serial integration projects and all five supported platforms.

## Additional info

### Matched measurements

Seconds below compare this draft’s baseline [38480898839](https://github.com/nickderobertis/printobserver/actions/runs/38480898839) with after run [38667838455](https://github.com/nickderobertis/printobserver/actions/runs/38667838455). All ten integration cells passed.

| Platform | Integration job: before → after (s) | test-integration step: before → after (s) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| linux-x86_64 | 1340 → 440 | 1288 → 388 |
| linux-aarch64 | 1368 → 438 | 1323 → 389 |
| macos-aarch64 | 2140 → 789 | 2021 → 614 |
| windows-x86_64 | 1948 → 1048 | 1816 → 902 |
| windows-aarch64 | 2041 → 1409 | 1869 → 1147 |

| Project | Linux x86 | Linux ARM | macOS | Windows x86 | Windows ARM |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| printobserver-octoprint | 63.1 → 10.0 | 62.0 → 10.0 | 74.3 → 18.0 | 62.3 → 16.0 | 61.7 → 19.6 |
| printobserver-server | 40.5 → 19.9 | 40.5 → 19.8 | 51.1 → 28.4 | 51.4 → 27.6 | 51.6 → 33.1 |
| printobserver-sdk | 71.7 → 11.2 | 82.9 → 11.0 | 285.5 → 15.4 | 153.1 → 17.7 | 122.7 → 22.4 |
| printobserver-sdk-python | 42.2 → 8.8 | 44.0 → 8.7 | 209.5 → 46.9 | 45.1 → 14.1 | 44.8 → 14.5 |
| printobserver-sdk-node | 40.0 → 6.9 | 41.2 → 7.8 | 183.0 → 8.0 | 39.9 → 9.7 | 40.0 → 10.4 |
| printobserver | 783.8 → 125.2 | 794.7 → 128.1 | 819.2 → 146.4 | 1204.8 → 607.0 | 1276.5 → 797.4 |
| octoprint-env | 246.3 → 206.1 | 257.1 → 203.5 | 398.0 → 350.2 | 258.2 → 208.1 | 270.4 → 248.0 |

| Gate | Before 38480898839 (s) | After 38667838455 (s) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| windows-x86_64 | 3904, passed | 2741, failed |
| windows-aarch64 | 5616, passed | 2901, failed |

The after gates rejected generated Node correspondence, subsequently repaired. These failed-run gate observations establish no speed gain or isolated effect attributable to this change.

The baseline is documentation-only commit `924b32f`, over `7233f04`/`f7b8897`; it changed nothing the tier runs. The paired after is `276a55d`. Both runs selected the seven projects listed above, with collected counts **1 / 1 / 5 / 5 / 5 / 19 / 62** on Linux and **1 / 1 / 5 / 5 / 5 / 19 / 58** on Windows. Windows environment results retain the existing **57 passed, 1 skipped**. No test was removed, newly skipped or moved off a platform. Project spans include compilation and world preparation: each extends from the preceding project’s last line to its own last line in the serial Nx stream; the first starts at the first Nx task. Nested timings are not added together.

The accepted comparison boundary is recorded in ruling 108:

> Ruling 108: option one. Report the paired before/after measurements from the identical-cohort runs you already have, as your gain evidence. Report the merged-tree CI separately as unpaired verification, attribute the four added CLI integration cases to PR 220 (merged at 0719ba3) by name, and make no like-for-like timing claim from the merged-tree run. No new baseline is required. The identical-count requirement applies to the paired runs, which you satisfied before the merge; merging main is what changed the count, not your change. Quote this ruling verbatim in the description so your judge reads it.

### Attribution and retained behavior

One-second dwells let the virtual printer reach command boundaries sooner. The hold remains **5400 seconds**: **5400 × G4 S1** replaces **540 × G4 S10**. The fixture test checks both total duration and maximum dwell. Existing duration, history, pause/resume/cancel and heat assertions remain; no timeout increases or immediate intervention retries were added. `confirming.rs` is unchanged relative to main. The CLI and environment reductions are recorded separately above; whole-job totals include cache and runner overhead and are not added to phase gains.

Preparation-only run [38606589148](https://github.com/nickderobertis/printobserver/actions/runs/38606589148), commit `70a84d6`, measured the preparation changes before faster pacing was restored. On the same integration selection, release-program cache hits cost **0–1 s**. Rust SDK spans fell **71.7 → 41 s** on Linux x86, **82.9 → 41 s** on Linux ARM, **153.1 → 42 s** on Windows x86 and **122.7 → 52 s** on Windows ARM. These measure reuse after cache hits, not elimination of cold compilation.

On macOS, diagnostic run [38556534832](https://github.com/nickderobertis/printobserver/actions/runs/38556534832) measured **35.02 s** in `ThreadingHTTPServer.server_bind → socket.getfqdn("127.0.0.1")` in each of 13 worlds. Other startup phases were below **0.4 s**, and uv’s process age was **0 s**. Removing that unused lookup preserves isolated real worlds. In the preparation-only run, the Mac job fell **2140 → 1640 s**, its integration step **2021 → 1504 s**, and SDK spans Rust **285.5 → 43 s**, Python **209.5 → 75 s**, Node **183.0 → 41 s**. Rust’s change combines cache reuse and lookup removal. These are historical preparation measurements, not final merged-tree Mac results or projections. Temporary lookup instrumentation was removed by `c6b8d2d`.

The release-program identity covers production crate sources, manifests/lockfile, declared and installed toolchain identity, profile configuration and compiler/profile environment variables. Each platform caches only `.release-program`; a restored executable must match its stored digest. Tests independently change source, toolchain and profile to prove rebuilding, and prove reuse with an unchanged key. They also cover corruption, inputs moving during a build, failed-build recovery, invalid compiler identity, workflow wiring and consumption by a real world.

Client worlds give the supervisor an empty PATH so an installed agent cannot accidentally run on a developer host. A real CLI/history journey proves isolation; no CI speedup is attributed to this change. Shared-printer suites remain serial, with no dependency edge making unrelated projects run integration. ETW, Windows command lookup, host caches and installer assertions are outside this change. The main merge imports [#220](https://github.com/nickderobertis/printobserver/pull/220) and [#221](https://github.com/nickderobertis/printobserver/pull/221) unchanged; their effects are excluded from the matched gain claims.

### Correctness repairs

Faster pacing exposed stale context during an open supervision turn. A new real-server HTTP journey first failed on the old implementation: status still showed feedrate **1.0** and omitted the intervention after accepting **1.2**. Status/context now gather current state. The journey checks operator and agent reads during the held turn, plus an out-of-bounds refusal recorded in history that leaves the accepted intervention unchanged. All **226 core journeys** and **11 binding journeys** passed.

The earlier local failure is retained in `tier.log`, mtime **12:45:50 UTC**. Its snapshot at **12:39:00.708** read target **199**, together with an intervention applied at **12:38:57.206** requesting **207**. The second intervention’s UUIDv7 timestamp was **12:39:00.795**, approximately **87 ms later**: the world had restored 199 between renderings. This is evidence of the stale-snapshot incident; the fresh-context regression and subsequent real-printer walks provide repair evidence.

One assertion correction is deliberate: two complete print listings failed equality only because `job_print_time_s` advanced **16 → 17**. The test now compares every other field exactly and separately requires both elapsed times to be nonnegative integers that never decrease. No retry or deadline changed. The focused real-server journey passed in **11.110 s**, followed by the whole tier.

Run **38626870981** also exposed the existing CLI shutdown race: the unchanged subprocess journey received **SIGTERM exit -15 instead of 0**. Readiness preceded installation of shutdown handlers. The CLI now polls the existing shutdown future before announcing readiness, handles an already-ready result, then awaits that same future. The original subprocess test passed locally in **35.10 s**, with unchanged output, assertions and deadline.

Credential subprocess journeys now bind port zero and use the server’s announced address, removing a reserve/drop race while retaining credential assertions. All **16** passed.

### Timeout diagnostics and cancellation evidence

After existing printer-state deadlines expire, Node, CLI and environment helpers invoke one internal diagnostic command. It gathers authenticated OctoPrint job/printer/connection reads, supervisor status where supplied, and at most **40 lines × 500 characters** from each of four logs. Serial logging is enabled. API keys, account passwords and supervisor credentials are redacted; longer secrets are masked first to handle overlapping prefixes. Diagnostics do not retry failed assertions or alter printer pacing. Their three HTTP calls have five-second transport timeouts; this is not a hard fifteen-second wall-clock guarantee.

The real Python subprocess case first failed against the old script with **exit 2: invalid choice diagnostics**, then passed with actual OctoPrint reads, bounded output, redaction and missing-record recovery. The existing Node journey verifies retained supervisor status and real endpoints. An isolated real-client probe outside the measured tier waited the full unchanged **180-second** deadline for an impossible state, emitted diagnostics, then successfully read the printer as printing. Output showed supervisor **printing**, OctoPrint **Printing**, bounded tails from all four logs and real serial Send/Recv traffic. The prefix-overlap regression failed before `ed2a9e7` because masking the short credential exposed the API-key suffix; it passes with complete redaction after that repair.

These tests prove diagnostics and recovery, not the cause or repair of the intermittent Windows ARM cancellation stall:

- **38626870981** failed with OctoPrint stuck in `Cancelling`; its **1472 s** failure is excluded from gain claims.
- Diagnostic run **38640286752** recorded all **42** `Cancelling → Operational` transitions completing in **0.004–2.039 s**, none unmatched. Its checksum resend followed the explicit `!!DEBUG:trigger_resend_checksum` negative probe. The stall did not recur, so those logs establish neither cause nor fix. Temporary upload conditions caused gate-policy failures and were removed.
- Cleanup run **38658971851**, Windows ARM job **116175417930**, reproduced the stall: **1294 s** whole job / **1112 s** step. Node exhausted its existing **180 s** operational wait, followed by CLI and environment timeouts. This was a persistent upstream state, not a normal two-second cancellation exceeding a one-second harness wait; `G4 S1` is fixture G-code.

Read-only history found every integration cell passing in the last eight completed main runs: **38480802906, 38264265864, 38223983289, 38214185640, 38198455080, 38177196189, 38149601011, 38129622038**. Both ten-second draft runs (**38480898839, 38606589148**) passed all cells. Six earlier one-second experiments (**38491102370, 38497487645, 38507428131, 38556534832, 38564734058, 38574539840**) passed Windows ARM; their sole integration failure was Windows x86 ETW at `traced.rs:453` in **38556534832**. None showed the stuck-state signature. That history does not establish that shorter dwells caused it.

The failing runs include the test-only credential-port repair and fresh-context change. The cleanup run additionally includes the elapsed-time assertion and startup-order repairs; the first stuck run predates the startup repair, so that cannot explain both failures. The environment suite reads `Cancelling` directly from OctoPrint, independently of supervisor context. No unsupported cancellation cause or fix is claimed.

### Generated correspondence repair

The matched after run **38667838455**, at `276a55d`, passed all five integration jobs but correctly rejected diagnostic assertions placed in a generated Node test. Commit `0a0525a` restores that file byte-for-byte and retains the assertions in the existing handwritten nine-step journey, reusing its status read. No generator, schema or enforcement rule changed. Eight targeted correspondence/repository cases passed in **120.81 s**, then the complete local integration tier passed again. Collection counts and original assertions remained intact. The later main merge changes the cohort and is reported separately below.

### Final merged-tree verification — unpaired

Gates and integration passed on both Linux and both Windows platforms, as did llmlint and pr-title. These are ten passing contexts; no final macOS pass is claimed. Neither the earlier Windows ARM logman failure nor the cancellation stall recurred, which does not establish a cancellation fix.

PR #220, merged at `0719ba3`, changes Linux CLI collection by net four (**19 → 23**). It adds `formats::parity_refuses_snapshots_that_keep_changing_through_the_existing_bound`, `formats::parity_survives_an_image_and_event_arriving_between_reads`, `traced::native_boundaries::a_descendant_connecting_after_its_parent_exits_is_observed`, `traced::native_boundaries::a_refused_attempt_from_the_real_command_is_observed`, `traced::native_boundaries::adjacent_invocations_do_not_inherit_each_others_endpoints`, `traced::native_boundaries::ipv6_accepted_and_refused_attempts_are_both_observed`, `traced::native_boundaries::the_real_commands_version_has_complete_empty_connection_evidence`, `traced::regression::connector`, and `traced::regression::each_invocation_observes_its_descendants_and_refused_attempts_only`. Both matched runs precede that upstream replacement.

### Local verification

On the final merged runtime, the whole seven-project real-OctoPrint tier passed locally with **1 / 1 / 5 / 5 / 5 / 23 / 62** tests. Kept-release-program tests passed **22/22 under -n 2**, **20.03 s**.

Rust formatting and scoped Clippy, changed Node formatting/lint/type checks, release-artifacts/environment Ruff format/lint and host/win32 type checks, workflow lint and repository-policy checks passed. No source changed after those checks. The inspected worktree is clean.

Earlier correctness evidence remains distinct from runner speed comparisons:

- Pre-merge judged lint passed **49 rules: 26 passed, 0 failed, 16 skipped, 7 not relevant**, history **20261015T050707Z-a8244**. The final merged-diff result supersedes that judgment.

Local judged lint used the documented `ONEHARNESS_HARNESSES=claude-code` override because the host’s configured Codex model was rejected by its ChatGPT login; repository harness configuration is unchanged.

An earlier npm-install case failed with exit 127, `asdf: command not found`. Subsequent same-shell runs on detached main and this branch both passed, so no causal host attribution is claimed. The case was not newly skipped and had passed all five release-artifacts CI cells in **38574539840**. In final run **38701061781**, Linux release-artifacts passed **447 cases with six existing skips**, including that unskipped Unix case. Windows passed **445 with eight existing skips**; the symlink-specific case already excludes Windows. Installer assertions are unchanged. The incompatible asdf just pin was recorded as an out-of-scope follow-up; local recipes used the existing just 1.58 without changing toolchain configuration.

### Workload and comparison boundaries

This draft’s baseline already collected **1127 Linux / 1094 Windows Rust tests**, 46/45 above that reference. The final run executed **1132 Rust tests per Linux host and 1101 per Windows host**, with three existing skips each: collected totals **1135 / 1104**. Compared with baseline run counts, growth is **5 / 7**: one server HTTP regression here and **4 / 6** from upstream tracing/parity work.

Final repo-checks collected **1513**: Linux **1513 passed**, Windows x86 **1465 passed / 48 skipped**, Windows ARM **1464 passed / 49 skipped**. Final release-artifacts collected **453**: Linux **447 passed / 6 skipped**, Windows **445 passed / 8 skipped**. PR #221 adds **99 repo-checks / 6 release-artifacts** cases over the pre-merge **1414 / 447** collections. Baseline Windows repo-checks were **1365 passed / 49 existing skips**. Relative to the spike, release-artifacts grew **424 → 447** through kept-build and machine-binding tests; the world-isolation journey adds one repo-e2e case, with platform-dependent baseline **337/338** and after **338/339**.

Main-group results were Linux x86 **339 passed / 2 skipped**, Linux ARM **335 / 6**, Windows x86 **317 / 22**, Windows ARM **314 / 24**; the release group’s one test passed on all four. Platform differences and upstream isolation/worker cases explain the growth. ### Suppression scope

## Measured: this change's own paired runs

All figures are in seconds and were read from this draft's own `ci` runs. Gate figures are the `gate (<platform>)` job's start to finish. Suite figures are each task's pytest session time as pytest reports it, which is a few seconds under the Nx task.

**Selection (identical in every run below).** Every gate cell ran `format-check`/`lint` for 24 projects, `typecheck` for 12, `test` for 20 projects plus 2 dependencies, `build` for 12, and `test-e2e` for project `repo-e2e` plus 1 dependency. A measurement-only `PYTEST_ADDOPTS` (now removed) left out the modules this change adds (`test_closures*`, `test_isolation*`, `test_worker_share*`), so before and after collected the same tests:

| platform | repo-checks | release-artifacts | repo-e2e |
|---|---|---|---|
| linux-x86_64 | 1414 | 424 | 339 |
| linux-aarch64 | 1414 | 424 | 339 |
| macos-aarch64 | 1414 | 424 | 337 |
| windows-x86_64 | 1414 (48 skipped) | 424 | 337 |
| windows-aarch64 | 1414 (49 skipped) | 424 | 336 |

**Runs**
- **before**: [38556419344](https://github.com/nickderobertis/printobserver/actions/runs/38556419344), attempts 1 and 2, on commit e6d9e27: main plus the measurement configuration, with this change taken out.
- **D**: [38591562924](https://github.com/nickderobertis/printobserver/actions/runs/38591562924), attempts 1 and 2, on 55757b4: this change with sizing rule D.
- **after (final rule, E2)**: [38636781226](https://github.com/nickderobertis/printobserver/actions/runs/38636781226), attempts 1 and 2, on 07ba9d9.

On Linux, D and E2 behave identically: the test tier runs 1+1 workers and e2e runs 4. That is why D's runs count as the same code on Linux. On Windows, D ran the test tier at 2+1 workers.

### Gate job

| platform | before a1, a2 → mean | after (E2) a1, a2 → mean | D a1, a2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| windows-x86_64 | 3889, 3351 → **3620** | 2558, 3450 → **3004** | failed (ETW) ×2 |
| windows-aarch64 | 4995, 6399 → **5697** | 5108, 4737 → **4923** | 5130, failed (ETW) |
| macos-aarch64 | 1811, 2083 → **1947** | 1864, a2 queued (see below) | 1887, 1940 |
| linux-x86_64 | 1051, 1385 → **1218** | 1323, 1275 → 1299; with D: **1245** | 1044, 1338* |
| linux-aarch64 | 988, 1011 → **1000** | 944, 945 → **945** | 951, 986 |

### repo-e2e (`test-e2e`)

| platform | before → mean | after (E2) → mean | D |
|---|---|---|---|
| windows-x86_64 | 1074, 933 → **1004** | 763, 953 → **858** | — |

### release-artifacts (`test`)

\* D a2's linux-x86_64 gate failed in `test_server_shutdown_journey` (SIGTERM → -15). The server prints `serving on` before it installs its stop handlers. That race is in the product, not in this change, and a follow-up has been drafted. Its e2e figure is the full session.

**macOS, attempt 2 of the final rule.** `gate (macos-aarch64)` of 38636781226 attempt 2 (job 116157215726) was still **queued** for a hosted macOS runner when the manager ruled not to wait for it. The push of 33387ce then superseded that attempt. macOS's after figure is attempt 1, alongside D's two runs, which are the same code on macOS.

**linux-x86_64 is within variance, not a regression and not a gain** (manager's ruling). Its four after runs (E2 ×2, D ×2) average 1245 s gate and 778 s e2e, against 1218 and 744 before. Runs of the same code spread over 1044–1385 s for the gate and 631–907 s for e2e, which is far wider than either difference. On Linux this change runs the test tier at main's worker counts with less copying. Its only e2e change caches one `git ls-files` per worker, and linux-aarch64 with the same code is faster on every measure.

### What each change bought, and where

- **Closure copies in repo-checks** (2e9bbda, 11f6f6a): the main gain. Serially (1 worker, the final rule), repo-checks fell from 937 to 483 s on windows-x86_64, from 2098 to 695 s on windows-aarch64, from 1115 to 820 s on macOS and from 451 to 373 s on linux-aarch64. On linux-x86_64 it moved from 676 to 643 s, within that cell's spread.
- **Windows gate**: 3620 → 3004 s on x86_64 and 5697 → 4923 s on aarch64 (measured means). The Windows test tier's critical path is the Rust `printobserver` crate (about 40 min), not the Python suites, so these gains show up through less contention and a shorter e2e more than through the test target.
- **repo-e2e on Windows** (dd5a7d9, one git listing per worker): 1004 → 858 s on x86_64 and 2472 → 1911 s on aarch64, at the same 3 workers. The aarch64 before spread (1996–2948 s) is wide, so the size of that gain is less certain than its direction.
- **xdist in the test tier**: measured, and **not kept on any CI cell**. In D, Windows ran repo-checks on 2 workers (338–467 s, against 360–728 s serially under E2). But with 2+1 workers beside the Rust journeys' NT Kernel Logger, `logman` refused its session ("No more data is available") in every Windows x86 run and on Windows aarch64's re-run, and in neither before run. Under E2 both Windows cells pass. On macOS/Linux, test-tier workers taken beside e2e lengthened e2e: rule B gave linux-x86_64 e2e 779 s and linux-aarch64 655 s, against 631 and 534 s before (runs 38556419344 a1 and 38566907789). An even three-way split left macOS e2e on 1 worker, and that gate went from 1834 to 2816 s (38480620735 → 38508602716). The suites still run under pytest-xdist and size through one shared function; on CI that function now answers 1 for the test tier.
- **Stand-in build race and stable collection IDs** (486269e, the id repairs): correctness, no duration change claimed.
- Projections are none. Every figure above is a measured run.

## The finished tree's own run

[38663726406](https://github.com/nickderobertis/printobserver/actions/runs/38663726406) on 33387ce, which carries no measurement configuration, was read once at 02:35 UTC. `gate` passed on all five platforms (linux-x86_64, linux-aarch64, macos-aarch64, windows-x86_64, windows-aarch64). `integration` passed on linux-x86_64, linux-aarch64, windows-x86_64 and windows-aarch64. `llmlint` (the judged lint over this diff) and `pr-title` passed. `integration (macos-aarch64)` (job 116190697732) was still **in progress** at that read. `supply-chain`, which is not a required check, fails on RUSTSEC-2026-0346/0347/0348, as it does on every branch.

## What

- `tools/repo-checks/src/repo_checks/workers.py` is now the one worker-sizing owner, imported by `repo-checks`, `release-artifacts` and `repo-e2e` (the old `tests/repo-e2e/tests/workers.py` is gone). It takes the host's logical processors bounded by memory at 2 GiB a worker. The end-to-end tier, its own Nx invocation, keeps that whole budget. Where the justfile runs it beside the test tier (non-Windows), or where the test tier traces the whole system (Windows), each test-tier suite takes one worker. Elsewhere the two test-tier suites divide the budget at `nx.json`'s parallelism. Each run says its choice and the figures behind it on standard error. Worker coverage is saved per worker and combined by `just coverage`, with floors unchanged.
- `repo-checks` copies each check's input closure, or reuses one immutable session snapshot with private mutable copies, instead of the whole tree per test. It keeps untracked non-ignored files, deletions, symlinks and `SchemaTreeLock`, and concurrent real processes prove nothing leaks between copies.
- `release-artifacts` builds its compiled stand-in once per source and toolchain under a content name, publishing it atomically and reusing it read-only, and it packages the client into private destinations. Real concurrent builders prove one whole program and identical crates.
- Stable collection IDs for timestamped archives (`test_verified_download.py`) and random tokens (`test_tracking.py`). Serial and xdist runs collect the same identities.
- `repo-e2e` asks git for the tree's listing once per worker.
- `ci.yml` and the recipes are as on main. The measurement-only configuration was removed in 33387ce.

## Why

The Python suites were the longest part of the Windows test tier: repo-checks held a Windows gate for 30–43 minutes against 9 on Linux. Cutting what each test copies gives that time back without loosening any assertion or timeout or dropping any test.

## Reference workload (spike-windows-gate-breakdown)

The spike measured a tree of 24 projects, 12 Rust crates (1,049 Windows tests; 1,081 Linux), 1,368–1,371 repo-checks tests, 424 release-artifacts tests, 337 end-to-end journeys and 7 integration projects. The client walk traces 776 invocations and the integration walk 276. Windows and Linux runners report 4 processors and macOS 3, as this change's runs confirm. Today's counts, collected serially on the finished tree: repo-checks **1510** (1414 at main, which grew by 43 with #219's `test_runner_temp.py`, plus 96 in this change's new isolation, closure and worker-share modules), release-artifacts **430** (424 plus 6 isolation tests), repo-e2e **341** (340 plus 1 isolation journey). The measured runs above use the 1414 / 424 / 336–339 selection on both sides.

## Notes for review

- Out-of-scope findings were drafted as follow-ups: the server's stop-handler race; `logman`'s ETW refusal (also seen on another branch without this change, and owned by client-journey-windows-cost-2); and the new rustls advisories RUSTSEC-2026-0346/0347/0348, which fail `supply-chain` (not a required check) on every branch.
- Locally, `release-plz` drafting journeys time out at 120 s when this shared host's load average is around 40–80. main fails the same way under that load. On CI they pass.

## What / Why

Keep one native ETW helper per test process and acquire/start, then stop/release the reserved kernel logger per invocation. This removes repeated logman/tracerpt subprocess setup and decoding while allowing other nextest processes to trace between calls. `traced(...) -> Ran` and its endpoint semantics are preserved. No shipped server/store/socket code, existing compared field/value, timeout, deadline, coverage floor or workflow context is changed.

Before returning, flush/rotate and synchronously decode finite closed ETL chunks with native ProcessTrace, then stop/decode the tail. Reconstruct process lifetimes, ancestry and endpoints from the combined QPC order of all native records for the invocation. Refuse missing ends, lost buffers, malformed/unclosed/corrupt tracing or controller failure. A named host-global mutex works independently of TEMP and recovers only this harness's reserved logger. TDH reads the actual provider manifests, including unsuccessful TCP connect requests. The helper's versioned private IPC golden deliberately advances to version 2: `controller_guid` identifies the persistent helper, not a persistent kernel lease.

A safe Rust dependency was evaluated: ferrisetw 1.2.0 closes its consumer before STOP and exposes no flush/file-switch or events-lost API, so the manager authorized the test-only C# SDK bridge. Rust unsafe_code remains forbidden. Exact SDK size/offset checks and real native calls run on both Windows arches.

Only the two new orphan-dependent cases (`regression::each_invocation_observes_its_descendants_and_refused_attempts_only` and `native_boundaries::a_descendant_connecting_after_its_parent_exits_is_observed`) and their helpers compile out on macOS. Every Windows/Linux scenario and assertion is retained. The cfg comments state the gap and name the follow-up.

The macOS interposer reads its activity file after the root exits and has no descendant-exit signal, so a delayed descendant with closed output pipes can be missed. Own CI38473950072 showed the empty endpoint set; a temporary real-interposer test on Linux reproduced it (nextest60739393-7985-45da-89f5-31eac1ebb9fc), then was removed per the ruling. This gap is **not fixed** here. Follow-up **drafts:printobserver-s-Windows-gates-and-every-integration-job-fit-in-30-minutes/drafts/20261015T025150Z-observe-macos-descendants-that-outlive-their-roo** records interposer.rs/interposer.c evidence and the suggested inherited lifecycle socket. The unused BTreeSet import left by those cfgs is now guarded by the matching cfg; no compiler warning is suppressed.

No directive or suppression was added by the final cfg/parity repairs. The existing connector fixture directive and all retained native directives are accounted for above. The new AssertUnwindSafe site states its invariant: the closure only reads real commands and appends fixture events, the World is discarded after refusal, and no partially completed comparison is reused.

## What

Route Windows x86 CI temporary files through writable, job-owned D: scratch before bootstrap, with a usable fallback and ownership-checked cleanup. Use PowerShell Core for Windows OctoPrint process lookup. Stabilize the history-format journey by comparing renderings of the same event sequence.

## Why

Windows filesystem and process-start costs multiply across thousands of test processes, keeping Windows gates much slower than other platforms. The previous process lookup also approached its timeout on Windows ARM. Reducing these shared costs speeds gate and integration work without reducing coverage or changing build profiles.

## Additional info

**Measured results.** This PR’s paired runs are [before 38423161634](https://github.com/nickderobertis/printobserver/actions/runs/38423161634) (`8a83374`) and [after 38440915234](https://github.com/nickderobertis/printobserver/actions/runs/38440915234) (`3e2487c`). Actual Nx project lists, commands and per-suite selected counts match within each architecture. These are observations from one pair, not projections.

| Measurement | windows-x86_64 before → after | windows-aarch64 before → after |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| gate job | 5,204 → 3,414 s | 6,135 → 5,756 s |
| integration job | 2,145 → 1,942 s | 2,602 → 2,060 s |
| gate `just check` step | 5,065 → 3,277 s | 5,781 → 5,562 s |
| repo-checks task, 1,413 selected | 4,203.65 → 1,670.61 s | 4,688.26 → 4,498.01 s |
| e2e parallel stage | 3,510.10 → 1,790.60 s | 3,659.79 → 3,416.22 s |
| real `command_of` completed-query median | 0.418034 → 0.391407 s | 22.691779 → 0.433706 s |
| integration `just test-integration` step | 1,921 → 1,803 s | 2,200 → 1,891 s |
| integration octoprint-env suite, 60 selected | 388.50 → 256.05 s | 618.84 → 275.46 s |
| integration `just octoprint-down` step | 1 → 1 s | 24 → 1 s |

Job IDs, before → after: gate x86 `115385526095` → `115446944558`; gate ARM `115385526149` → `115446944678`; integration x86 `115385526321` → `115446944715`; integration ARM `115385526426` → `115446944594`.

**Measurement boundaries.** Both runs temporarily used `E2E_BESIDE_TESTS=true`. Both Windows gate jobs failed the same temporary benchmark-step dispatch expectation after every selected parallel case finished. Outcomes match: x86 337 selected (314 pass, 22 skip, 1 fail); ARM 336 selected (311 pass, 24 skip, 1 fail). Neither reached the subsequent `alone` stage. These clocks include that common failure and are not passing whole-e2e verdicts. Both integration pairs passed, including identical octoprint-env outcomes of 59 pass/1 skip.

The finished tree removes the temporary benchmark step/helper and restores the base Windows `E2E_BESIDE_TESTS=false` schedule. Its exact dispatch regression passes locally. The experimental gate clocks do not establish the finished tree’s ordinary gate duration. The removed lookup benchmark itself took 5→2 s x86 and 122→3 s ARM; those reductions are included in the experimental job clocks and are not production savings.

On x86, repo-checks fell by 2,533.04 s and the e2e parallel stage by 1,719.50 s. These figures cover TEMP routing and pwsh together, not an isolated TEMP effect. The separate lookup comparison shows only a small x86 difference. After-run directory output and real child/tempfile tests confirm D: routing.

ARM retains its C: temp directory. Its completed lookup median fell from 22.691779 to 0.433706 s, while printer teardown fell from 24 to 1 s. Each benchmark starts a real child, checks its entire command line and attempts five reads: x86 completed 5/5 on both sides; ARM completed 4/5 before and 5/5 after. The remaining ARM before sample hit the unchanged 30 s bound at 30.031454 s. Medians include completed queries only; the censored sample is a lower bound.

No client-walk improvement is claimed. The successful gate client journey took 2,608.925→2,717.158 s x86 and 3,041.926→3,160.333 s ARM. CLI integration’s same 19 tests took 1,161.243→1,165.498 s x86 and 1,215.853→1,273.536 s ARM. Whole-job gains do not establish faster client bodies or separately measured process lifecycle costs.

**Behavior and scope.** TEMP/TMP are exported before bootstrap and subsequent children. Missing scratch drives or failed scratch creation fall back to existing usable temp; unusable paths fail clearly. Cleanup restores usable temp for post-job cache actions before removing only the job’s marked scratch, protecting unrelated files and refusing linked or foreign paths. ARM and other platforms keep their existing temp.

Windows lookup explicitly resolves `pwsh` and retains the Get-CimInstance `CommandLine` query, existing normalization and quote handling, ownership decisions, 30-second timeout, and missing/inaccessible/gone-process refusals. Missing PowerShell Core produces a recovery instruction in lookup and setup. No image-name or executable-path substitute is used.

The integration policy permits exactly `just runner-temp cleanup` under `always()` alongside printer teardown; tests reject broader conditional-step exceptions. All 12 required context names, platform selections and the release PR full sweep remain. The dispatcher implementation and integration/release-build harness are unchanged. No product output or shared interface changes.

**Identical measured selection.** Both Windows architectures in both runs execute format-check/lint for the same 24 projects, typecheck for the same 12, test for the same 20 plus two prerequisites, test-e2e for repo-e2e plus one prerequisite, and build for the same 12. The literal gate-tier command selects the full graph from the unowned workflow diff. Coverage, workflow lint and repository checks remain in the unchanged gate.

The shared project sets are:

- R, 12 Rust projects: printobserver-supervisor-api, printobserver-store-sqlite, printobserver-printer-api, printobserver-oneharness, printobserver-vision-api, printobserver-octoprint, printobserver-server, printobserver-obico, printobserver-types, printobserver-core, printobserver-sdk, printobserver.
- P, eight other test projects: printobserver-sdk-python, release-artifacts, contract-codegen, skilltest-wiring, printobserver-sdk-node, octoprint-env, printer-smoke, repo-checks.
- A, four other projects: skill-install, obico-env, skilltest, repo-e2e.

For both runs: format-check/lint = R+P+A; typecheck = P+A; test = R+P; build = R; test-e2e = repo-e2e. Prerequisites are printobserver-types:schemas and printobserver:build; the latter also precedes e2e. Schemas are separate from nextest counts.

Every measured suite’s selected count matches before/after, including skips. Rust nextest executes 1,094 tests with three additional skips under identical integration-binary exclusions. Per-crate run/skipped counts: supervisor-api 22/0, printer-api 33/0, vision-api 18/0, types 42/0, core 289/0, oneharness 57/0, octoprint 116/0, obico 51/0, store-sqlite 76/2, server 189/0, SDK 67/0, CLI 134/1. Python selections: contract-codegen 91, release-artifacts 424, octoprint-env gate 25, Python SDK 73, printer-smoke 106, skilltest-wiring 145, repo-checks 1,413. Node SDK selects 74. Parallel e2e selects 337 x86 / 336 ARM, with outcomes above.

Both integration runs execute `test-integration` sequentially for seven projects: printobserver-octoprint (1), printobserver-server (1), printobserver-sdk (5), printobserver-sdk-python (5), printobserver-sdk-node (5), printobserver (19), octoprint-env (60). Each architecture selects 96 tests. Bring-up/down recipes and selections are unchanged.

**Reference workload.** The [spike report](https://github.com/nickderobertis/printobserver/issues/212), with preserved harness `00c5e84`, records 24 projects, 12 Rust crates (1,049 Windows tests; 1,081 Linux), 1,368–1,371 repo-checks tests, 424 release-artifacts tests, 337 e2e journeys and seven integration projects. Client/integration walks trace 776/276 invocations; Windows/Linux report four processors and macOS three. This PR’s lookup logs report four processors on both Windows architectures; no new walk invocation count is claimed.

This PR’s measured Windows Rust count grows by 45: server 172→189, SDK 48→67, CLI 125→134. This branch changes no Rust product source; its one Rust change is the journey assertion site described below. Repo-checks grows from 1,371 by 39 TEMP tests and three workflow-policy tests to 1,413. One missing-tool recovery test was added after the comparison: finished-tree Linux collection records 1,414 repo-checks tests, including 40 TEMP tests, not another native performance measurement. E2e figures are architecture-specific parallel-stage selections, not whole-tier counts.

Reference evidence only: [run 38218849444](https://github.com/nickderobertis/printobserver/actions/runs/38218849444) paired D: TEMP on x86, measuring repo-checks 1,514→755 s, e2e 3,875→1,030 s and client 1,564→1,357 s. [Run 38200888322](https://github.com/nickderobertis/printobserver/actions/runs/38200888322) measured legacy/pwsh lookup at 0.42→0.39 s x86 and 22.7→0.47 s ARM. These figures belong to those cells, not final harness `00c5e84`; that harness has focused repaired-scenario verification and judged lint, not a claimed green broad finished-tree suite.

**Unchanged settings and remaining measurement gaps.** No Defender change is retained: x86 scanning was already off and ARM excludes C:/D:. Coverage reduction showed no useful runtime gain and is rejected. No Cargo profile, linker or incremental change is retained: dev/test keep #204’s no-debuginfo settings, release stays unchanged, and Rust/Python coverage floors measure the same code.

- **link-task-attribution-refused:** the preserved timed_linker records duration/output without task tokens or start/end timestamps, and measure.py combines tasks into one links.jsonl. Windows 60.0/56.6 s are summed linker process time overlapping compilation, not validated per-crate link wall time. Next step: validate task-tagged timestamped records and Cargo target identity on both Windows architectures before selecting a dependent linker/cache change.
- **body-lifecycle-separation-refused:** nextest durations include body and lifecycle without independent body entry/exit timestamps on either Windows architecture or Linux. The fastest-test proxy is rejected. Next step: coordinate temporary body timing with client-journey-windows-cost and measure identical real binaries on all three before a spawn fix.
- **build-settings-pair-refused:** spike comparisons are cold compile-only samples without paired runtime; rust-lld fallback was unverified and incremental-on/split-unpacked did not complete. Existing `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0` is a setting, not a comparison. Next step: verify effective compiler/linker arguments and paired compile AND runtime results on both Windows architectures before proposing rust-lld, line-tables-only, split-debuginfo or incremental changes.

**Cache and account evidence.** No cache change is retained; cache configuration stays as the base carries it. The paired runs already restore full compatible Windows Rust-cache matches with existing keys and bounded save scope: x86 restores 1,055,218,415 bytes under `v0-rust-gate-Windows_NT-x64-6233a5ee-59a535ac`; ARM restores 781,835,343 bytes under `v0-rust-gate-Windows_NT-arm64-217789c5-59a535ac`. Spike-era misses and duplicate Linux keys do not establish a useful new restriction. Release-build reuse remains with integration-tier-cost and its harness is untouched.

Account evidence identifies a personal User account with an undisclosed purchased ceiling. Observing 25 concurrent jobs establishes only a lower bound; Free/Pro defaults of 20/40 and five shared macOS slots do not establish entitlement. No host/shard allocation or paid larger-runner recommendation is made.

**Regression repairs and evidence.** [Run 38456931419](https://github.com/nickderobertis/printobserver/actions/runs/38456931419) on `9472cd7` failed `gate (windows-aarch64)` and `gate (macos-aarch64)`. The resulting repairs are:

- **History-format race on Windows ARM.** `formats.rs:181` found different field sets in the two renderings of `history --print-id … --limit 7`: the JSON read named one event and the text read named seven or more. The same failure occurs on `main`: [run 38264265864](https://github.com/nickderobertis/printobserver/actions/runs/38264265864), job `114862323787`. `formats::run` calls `world.wants` before each read and may restart the print; start-of-print events containing `interval_s`, an image, and `detail`/`site` can arrive between reads. Commit `512f83c` takes at most five history pairs, without sleeps, until both renderings name the same ordered `events.N.id` sequence. The existing field-set and value assertions then run on that pair, with `--limit 7` unchanged. Matching IDs with differing fields still fail immediately; exhausted attempts report every pair of ID lists. No CLI flag was added, and the tracing harness is untouched. The affected journey passed within the Linux journeys binary in 381 s; Windows ARM execution remains the platform-specific proof.
- **macOS temp-test environment.** macOS runners set `TMPDIR`, which Python’s tempfile reads before `TEMP`, through the `/var` symlink that runner-temp refuses. Windows runners set none. Commit `68d5c45` gives these tests a TMPDIR-free environment matching Windows; the script is unchanged. With local TMPDIR set to a symlinked directory, the previous test file reproduces the failure and the repaired file passes 40/40.
- **macOS lookup-test image identity.** Homebrew framework Python re-executes as `Python.app`, so `ps` reports that image rather than the venv’s python. The test now requires an image followed by every argument exactly, including quotes. Forcing command_of to return image-only `ps -o comm=` output fails the test with `got 'python'`.

The history comparison’s field/value assertions and existing deadlines remain unchanged; the bounded retry applies only when the two reads observed different event sequences.

**Recorded verification.** Commit `9472cd7` removes all measurement-only configuration and files. Verification at that point included 151 targeted tests passing in 171.24 s: real child/tempfile routing and fallback, ownership-safe cleanup, full command-line lookup over a real child, bring-down refusal of an unrelated live child, and the copied-workflow dispatch regression. The missing-pwsh recipe test first failed for the intended command-not-found reason and passed after the guard was added. Windows runs exercise Windows APIs; Linux checks establish shared behavior and typing, not execution of the Windows lookup branch.

Changed-file formatting/lint, native and win32 typing, targeted workflow checks and workflow lint passed. Judged lint `20261013T175649Z-b550a` recorded 49 rules: 23 pass, zero fail, 16 skip and 10 not relevant.

After the repairs above, recorded checks include test_runner_temp.py (40 passed), the octoprint-env lookup test, ruff format/check, native and win32 ty checks for octoprint-env, cargo fmt and clippy with warnings denied for printobserver. The journeys binary was also run: the repaired history journey passed, while `watching::an_adjustment_under_the_detectors_pause_earns_a_resume_after_the_grace` failed a timing bound under parallel load and passed alone. That failure is recorded as a follow-up and is not changed here; the full journeys run is not claimed green. Final judged lint `20261013T210508Z-dd843` recorded 49 rules: 21 pass, zero fail, 16 skip and 12 not relevant. The final diff adds, moves or rewrites no suppression and changes no statement covered by a site suppression.

Earlier failure evidence remains separate from the paired comparison. Baseline Linux job `115385526166`, log lines 5547–5568, showed PowerShell’s decorated exception output splitting the exact recovery message. The finished catch writes the error/recovery directly to stderr and exits 1. Local PowerShell 7.6.6 did not reproduce the old wrapping with longer paths or narrow columns; the CI failure supplies the regression evidence, not a claimed local red test.

In [run 38410239426](https://github.com/nickderobertis/printobserver/actions/runs/38410239426), x86 job `115341272635` failed the client format comparison after 722.178 s, and relay partial-input also failed. Those failures were reported to their owners. The relay harness is unchanged; the client format comparison is repaired as described above. Both paired Windows client journeys passed.

Recorded follow-ups cover inherited release-artifact over-selection, manual routing, scratch ancestor-Git isolation and virtualenv-prefix noise. The finished tree’s ordinary CI duration is not inferred from the experiment; no 1,800-second verdict or external merge is claimed.

## What

**Spike only — never merged.** `spike-windows-gate-breakdown` measures, cause by cause on GitHub's real runners, where the time of the two Windows gate cells and of every `integration (<platform>)` job goes. This branch's `ci.yml` is replaced by an experiment matrix. The harness is the `gate-spike` project at `tools/gate-spike/`. `just spike-measure <experiment> <targets> <out>` runs one experiment over one target set and writes per-test and per-Nx-task durations to `<out>/measure.json`. `just spike-cell` is what each cell runs, and `just spike-harness-test` runs the harness's own tests. The report is the document `spike-windows-gate-breakdown-report` of project `authoring:windows-gate-thirty-2026-10-12`.

## Why

A Windows gate takes 70–103 minutes, and the macOS and Windows integration jobs take 30–39, against a 30-minute target. The plan's fixes need a measured cause each.

## Runs

Every figure in the report comes from these runs. Ids are GitHub Actions run ids, read with `gh run view <id> --json jobs`, the jobs API and the job logs; no run was re-run, cancelled or dispatched.

| Run | Commit | Cells and what each measured |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [38200888322](https://github.com/nickderobertis/printobserver/actions/runs/38200888322) | c0c597d | **windows-x86_64 and windows-aarch64** (9 cells each): `rust-baseline`, `rust-nocov` and `rust-defender` measure all 12 crates' `test` tasks with coverage, without it, and with Defender exclusions (compile, run, per test, links, every client-command journey operation). `rust-levers` measures cold `compile-only` builds of `printobserver:test` at baseline, line-tables-only, debug-0 and rust-lld. `py-baseline` measures every Python `test` task. `py-coverage`, `py-xdist` and `py-defender` measure repo-checks without coverage and with sysmon, at xdist 2/3/4, and with Defender exclusions plus the end-to-end tier. `e2e` measures the octoprint-env lookup benchmark, Defender's state and the end-to-end tier. **linux-x86_64**: `rust-baseline`, `rust-nocov`, and `py` (every Python suite, coverage levers, xdist 2/3/4). **spike-integration** on all 5 platforms: each `test-integration` project, plus the lookup benchmark on Windows. This run's Python cells ran on the spike's own tree (103 repo-checks and 16 end-to-end tests failed because the spike changes `ci.yml` and `justfile`), and windows-2025's C: drive filled up in `py-coverage`. |
| [38210204156](https://github.com/nickderobertis/printobserver/actions/runs/38210204156) | c32cbcd | Paired cells under `base-tree` (the base branch's `ci.yml` and `justfile` in place for the run). **windows-x86_64**: `py-nocov`, `py-sysmon`, `py-xdist-2/3/4`, `py-temp-on-d` (repo-checks baseline against the lever on the same runner) and `e2e`. **windows-aarch64**: the same without `py-temp-on-d`. **linux-x86_64** `py`: every repo-checks lever, plus release-artifacts at xdist-4. **spike-integration** on all 5 platforms, a second sample. The xdist-3 cells, windows-2025's xdist-2/-4 cells and windows-11-arm's xdist-4 cell died partway because the output directory sat inside the copied tree; run 38218849444 re-measured them. |
| [38218849444](https://github.com/nickderobertis/printobserver/actions/runs/38218849444) | f79e5a9 | **windows-x86_64**: repo-checks baseline against xdist-2, xdist-3 and xdist-4; against TEMP on D:; TEMP on D: against TEMP on D: with xdist-3; the end-to-end tier on C: against D:; `printobserver:test` on C: against D:. **windows-aarch64**: repo-checks baseline against xdist-3 and xdist-4. |
| [38243471110](https://github.com/nickderobertis/printobserver/actions/runs/38243471110) | 591e0e5 | `harness (windows-x86_64/-aarch64)`: the harness's own tests on both Windows runners. 6 and 8 failures, all fixed. |
| [38253891231](https://github.com/nickderobertis/printobserver/actions/runs/38253891231) | fbc6b5b | The harness's tests again: 1 failure each, fixed. One of them showed windows-11-arm keeps real-time scanning on after `Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring`. |
| [38263332486](https://github.com/nickderobertis/printobserver/actions/runs/38263332486) | a670381 | The harness's tests: passed on both. |
| [38272876347](https://github.com/nickderobertis/printobserver/actions/runs/38272876347) | cd44779 | Harness validation at cd44779: both Windows cells passed; this adds no performance figures. |


The baseline compared against is the gate-thirty-minutes draft's runs [38181620797](https://github.com/nickderobertis/printobserver/actions/runs/38181620797) and [38188847711](https://github.com/nickderobertis/printobserver/actions/runs/38188847711). The branch's last commit carries `[skip ci]`: its workflow is the experiment matrix as measured, plus the harness job, and was not run a further time.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Evidence limits: the report marks rust-lld fallback figures invalid as linker-effect evidence and labels supervisor-internal I/O/socket timings, exact account concurrency entitlements, and body-subtracted spawn costs as open. Projections are conditional estimates; the plan's nodes will re-measure each lever.

The final local harness repairs are c9ae429: duration validation, stale-report removal, spaced executable attribution, recursive-copy accounting, typed identity aliases, and stderr failure verdicts. Native-boundary and required-linker refusal proof is ad60961; the Windows-only native checks have not been run in a new CI round.

00c5e84 finishes the local recovery proof: retained-temporary diagnostics, quiet summary behavior, control-character linker records, and structural task dispatch. Three focused checks passed, plus format/lint and Linux/Windows type checks. These commits all carry `[skip ci]`.

Finished-tree judged lint is green on 00c5e84 (20261012T173021Z-f68d1: 28 passed, 0 failed). Workflow lint, static suppression validation, format/lint and Linux/Windows type checks are green.

That scenario was re-run on the finished tree afterward and passed (1 passed, 9.51 s); the broad run is not represented as a green final-tree suite. c48.body:
## What

Expose spool management, remaining filament, pending charges, paginated printer history and read-only preflight checks through the server, derived CLI and generated Rust, Python and Node clients. Add at-a-glance spool summaries, configurable filament checks with actionable rejection messages and an explicit override, startup accounting for unseen prints, and skill documentation with worked examples.

## Why

Operators need to know what filament remains and why before an hours-long print runs dry. Giving operators and supervising agents the same contract, grants and audit trail keeps spool tracking accessible and every change accountable.

## Additional info

- **Upgrade:** Existing configurations are not modified. Add `register_spool`, `load_spool`, `unload_spool`, `adjust_spool` and `retire_spool` to the `operator` row of `[safety.actions]`, then restart the service. Until then, spool mutations are refused with `actor_may_not_request`. Leave the agent’s grants unchanged; new installation templates grant the operator all five and the agent none.
- The optional `[spools]` table controls preflight mode (`refuse`, `warn` or `off`), buffer and analysis wait. Defaults are `refuse`, a buffer of the larger of 10% of required filament or 5 g, and a 300-second analysis wait. An operator can override a refused start with `--override-filament-check true`.
- **Breaking API change:** The server’s public operation arrays and declaration types expand; the generated operation description advances to version 2 to represent repeatable query parameters. HTTP routes remain under `/v1`.

## What

Release all twelve crates together at one version, with shared internal dependency requirements, so changes touching only some crates can draft a valid release. Required-gate journeys cover partial releases, and workflow checks protect reporting that opens or updates a `release-broken` issue on drafting or publishing failure, then closes it when both succeed.

## Why

No release has shipped since v0.3.0, leaving subsequent fixes and features—including spool tracking—unavailable to installers and projects waiting to adopt them. Keeping versions aligned restores the release path; tracking failures with run links makes the next break visible instead of letting it go unnoticed for days.
